tagline: A thousand-year-old stupa, Ai Khai of Wat Chedi, shadow-puppet cafes, and waterfalls plus the Gulf coast
introHtml:
Nakhon Si Thammarat, which southerners just call Mueang Khon, is an old city built around the Phra Borommathat stupa since ancient times. People come to pray at the stupa, to visit Ai Khai of Wat Chedi who is famous across the country, and to walk the cultural street where the old-town feel lingers alongside shadow-puppet craft and nielloware.

The province is large and has it all, mountains and sea. There are waterfalls and the Khao Luang forest to the west, and beaches plus Khanom with its pink dolphins on the Gulf side. The food is bold southern Thai all over town, from morning khanom jeen to southern curry-and-rice shops with a dozen dishes to choose from.
bestTime: December–April for clear skies, easy beach and waterfall trips; the heavy rains run October–December, best avoided

highlights.name: Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan
highlights.blurb: The great Phra Borommathat stupa that is the heart of the city. Locals hold it in deep respect and come to pray and view the relics in the hall. It is the first thing that comes to mind when you mention this province.

highlights.name: Ai Khai, Wat Chedi
highlights.blurb: An image of a temple boy that people believe grants wishes. Crowds come from all over the country to ask for luck in fortune and work, and the stalls around the temple sell offerings like roosters, firecrackers, and toy soldier outfits.

highlights.name: Khanom district and the pink dolphins
highlights.blurb: The province's northern coast, where you can take a boat out to see pink dolphins. There are quiet beaches, Koh Nui Nok, and the Khao Phlai Dam viewpoint. This is the seaside people like to stay on.

highlights.name: The cultural street and old town
highlights.blurb: The Tha Mon quarter and the area around the old city wall still show old buildings, the city pillar shrine, and shops selling Nakhon nielloware. It is the part of town for strolling, eating, and soaking up the Mueang Khon mood.

highlights.name: Shadow puppetry and Nakhon nielloware
highlights.blurb: Nakhon is the home of nang talung shadow puppets and the manora dance. The Suchart shadow-puppet house lets you watch puppets being made, while Nakhon nielloware is the province's renowned black-inlaid silverwork.

highlights.name: Waterfalls and the Khao Luang range
highlights.blurb: The western side of the province is the Khao Luang forest, with several waterfalls like Krung Ching, Phrom Lok, and Ai Khiao, good for a swim and a hike on days when you want to skip the sea.

foodScene.name: Mueang Khon khanom jeen
foodScene.note: The city's signature breakfast, fresh noodles eaten with nam ya, nam prik, taipla curry, and green curry, with a big pile of fresh veg on the side. The famous shops open early and people line up.

foodScene.name: Southern curry and rice
foodScene.note: Curry shops line up a dozen dishes in trays, taipla curry, kaeng lueang, khua kling, stir-fried chili, properly bold southern flavors, ladled over one plate of rice to fill you up. You find it all over town.

foodScene.name: Taipla curry and khua kling
foodScene.note: Bold local southern dishes, taipla curry rich and salty-spicy, while khua kling pork or beef is fragrant with curry paste. Eaten with hot steamed rice and fresh vegetables.

foodScene.name: Seafood on the Khanom and Pak Phanang coasts
foodScene.note: Both coasts sit on the Gulf, so fish, squid, shrimp, and blue crab come in fresh. The seaside shops around Khanom and Pak Phanang cook it many ways, and there are shrimp paste and dried seafood to take home.

foodScene.name: Southern-style roti and pulled tea
foodScene.note: The southern tea-shop culture, roti crisp outside and soft inside with hot pulled tea, a breakfast and snack the locals sit over and chat at their leisure.

foodScene.name: Coffee and cafes in town
foodScene.note: Mueang Khon has a lot of new cafes, both shops in old buildings in the old quarter and cafes with mountain views. Coffee lovers can drop in to relax and find plenty of angles for photos.

foodScene.name: Khanom la and local sweets
foodScene.note: Khanom la, crisp-fried lacy threads, is a famous treat, in both crisp and soft versions, sold as gifts alongside other southern local sweets at markets and souvenir shops.

foodScene.name: Fruit and Mueang Khon gifts
foodScene.note: Khiriwong mangosteen, pomelo, and lime are the local fruits, while the popular souvenirs are khanom la, Nakhon nielloware, and shrimp paste from Pak Phanang.

attractions.name: Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan
attractions.blurb: The temple with the great Phra Borommathat stupa in the city center, a place to pray and view relics, regarded as the center of faith for Nakhon people.

attractions.name: Wat Chedi (Ai Khai)
attractions.blurb: The temple where crowds come to ask Ai Khai for luck in fortune and work. The grounds buzz with offering stalls of roosters, firecrackers, and toy soldier outfits. It sits in Sichon district.

attractions.name: Khanom district
attractions.blurb: The province's northern seaside, where you take a boat to see pink dolphins, visit quiet beaches, and climb the Khao Phlai Dam viewpoint for a wide look over the bay.

attractions.name: Ban Khiriwong
attractions.blurb: A village at the foot of Khao Luang known for good air, clear streams, and mangosteen. Stroll by the water, soak your feet, and try local food. It is a popular spot to unwind.

attractions.name: Krung Ching Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A big waterfall in the Khao Luang park area, with the lovely Nan Nuan Kaeo tier. A short hike in lets you swim and enjoy the nature.

attractions.name: The cultural street and city pillar shrine
attractions.blurb: The old-town quarter around the city pillar shrine and city wall, for strolling past old buildings, nielloware shops, and local food in the Mueang Khon atmosphere.

attractions.name: Suchart shadow-puppet house
attractions.blurb: A shadow-puppet museum where you can watch puppets being carved and performed, a living place to learn southern folk art.

attractions.name: Laem Talumphuk and Pak Phanang
attractions.blurb: The Gulf coast in the south of the province, with a long sandy beach, fishing communities, and seafood markets. A good stop to eat seafood and see coastal life.

itineraryIdeas: Nakhon Si Thammarat 2D1N — the stupa, Ai Khai of Wat Chedi, southern curry and rice
Nakhon Si Thammarat for luck-seekers — the stupa, Ai Khai, the city pillar shrine
Nakhon Si Thammarat for nature — Khiriwong, Krung Ching Waterfall, Khao Luang
Nakhon Si Thammarat for the sea — Khanom for pink dolphins, Khao Phlai Dam
Nakhon Si Thammarat for cafes and the old town — the cultural street, old-building cafes
Nakhon Si Thammarat to Surat Thani — visit Ai Khai then on to Cheow Lan Reservoir
